messages:
mia: Heads up — cost dashboard showing negative prefetch credits for tenant `acme-inc` today. Not a huge amount but skews per-model unit econ. Anyone else seeing this?
orson: I saw something similar in the staging slice last night. Looks like a race between cache attribution and rollback logic.
praveen: Can you paste an example trace? I want to see the path: prefetch -> hotpath -> cache-hit attribution.
mia: Pasted a simplified trace below. Note the prefetch id is reused across two chain calls.

mia: ```
trace_id: t-9a1
requests: [
  {id: p1, type: prefetch, model: llama-small, cache_key: k123},
  {id: h1, type: hotpath, model: gpt-medium, depends_on: p1, cache_hit: true}
]
metrics: {prefetch_cost: 0.03, hotpath_cost_saved: 0.05}
```

anya: If prefetch credits are deducted and then hotpath also applies a saving we might be double-counting the saving but only one side gets credited. We should ensure credits are idempotent per cache_key + window.
orson: Agreed. Current rule is per-request attribution: the prefetch call writes a credit token, and the first subsequent cache hit consumes it. Edge case: if prefetch rolls back (timeout) after the hotpath already consumed the write, you end up with a refund + consumption.
praveen: Quick proposal: make credit tokens immutable once issued and use a TTL + consumer pointer; if rollback happens we mark refund but never allow negative net credits. Simpler: never emit refunds automatically — emit correction events and surface them in telemetry.
sam: I worry about long tail storage cost if we keep tokens immutable. Also UX: product teams see a spike then a correction — that's noisy. Can we batch corrections and mark them as preview adjustments in the dashboard? 
anya: Batch corrections is fine. We should also flag tenants with >X% correction rate. Then they can opt into stricter prefetch gating.
praveen: Also need telemetry: count of "stale-token-consumed" and "token-refund-emitted" per route, model, and tenant. Expose as a panel so console teams can triage.
mia: +1. Also need a clear rule for multi-model chains: which model gets the credit? Right now we attribute to the consumer model (hotpath), but the prefetching model owner expects credit.
orson: For chains we could split credit proportionally by token savings observed per model when the chain executed. But that's messy for UX. Alternative: attribute to the first model that wrote the token unless overridden by explicit route metadata.
sam: Can we add a small heuristic: if the prefetch and consumer belong to same tenant, credit prefetch; otherwise credit consumer. That would reduce cross-tenant surprises.
praveen: That heuristic seems reasonable but we should document it in chargeback rules. Also add a toggle in console: "Prefer writer crediting for same-tenant prefetches".
anya: Implementation note: update the attribution function in tokenizer_pipeline: replace current logic with:

anya: ```pseudo
// attribution(token)
if token.writer_tenant == consumer_tenant and feature_prefetch_writer_crediting on:
  credit = writer
else:
  credit = consumer
record(attribution_record(token_id, credit))
```

dev-bot: deploy queued: infra/attribution-fix -> canary-1 at 2026-03-20T10:32Z :rocket:

mia: For the dashboard, can we surface a new "prefetch correction" line in the token-savings waterfall and a tooltip that links to the raw event stream? That will make audits easier.
praveen: Yep. I'll add an API endpoint /admin/prefetch-corrections?tenant=&model=&since= to back the widget.
orson: One more edgecase: long-running sessions where prefetch tokens outlive model versions. We should include model-sku in token metadata so corrections can be attributed to the SKU at issue time.
sam: Good call. Otherwise billing and cost-of-goods mismatches happen during rollouts.
mia: Cool — action items: praveen add telemetry counters + admin endpoint; anya update attribution code with TTL and heuristic; ors on validate replay logic and integration test for rollback; sam add dashboard wire for prefetch-corrections and tooltip. I'll open individual tickets. :thumbsup:
